translation_notes: Identity translation: `expr` is a whole SPARQL clause -- upstream's three call sites pass 'bind("thing" as ?name)', 'bind(<http://example.org/other> as ?other)' and 'bind(:Thing as ?type)' -- received as a caller-supplied STRING and spliced by `%` formatting into the query text: `"select * where { ?s ?p ?o . %s } " % expr`. This is exactly the textual-assembly idiom the stratum targets, and it is out of reach by construction: s{ }'s interpolation ({expr}) is legal only in TERM position and lowers to initBindings, never to a substitution inside the query string -- there is no island for 'an entire clause held in a variable', the same limit noted for -{ }/m{ } in INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2, here on the read side and on a full query engine rather than a BGP island.

no partial credit either: `expr` is not decomposable into a fixed number of terms at the call site -- one call binds a plain literal, another an IRI, the third uses the `:` prefix declared in the query's own prologue -- so there is no fixed slot to interpolate even after the fact.
minimal excerpt showing the limit: `g.query("... select * where { ?s ?p ?o . %s } " % expr)` where `expr` is an opaque string parameter reused across differently-shaped BIND clauses.

`check` reads a free variable `g` set up by the enclosing (not extracted) get_bind_tests(); restored via a context shim (test_evaluate_bind_context.py) reproducing that single-triple graph, imported identically by both original.py and translated.ldpy.

driver: the three real invocations from get_bind_tests() (upstream, at the pinned commit) prove the (unmodified) region still computes right against the restored graph -- each exercises a differently-shaped `expr`, which is itself part of the argument that no fixed term slot could have covered this.
